sections.section: RULE - Kalat Division Reserved Trees Rules 1970
sections.description:
KALAT DIVISION RESERVED TREES RULES, 1970
KALAT DIVISION RESERVED TREES
RULES, 1970
[Gazette of Baluchistan,
Part I, 29th January 1971]
No. S. O. A. IV/28‑70/Forest.‑In
exercise of the Powers conferred on
him by section 32 read with sections 41 and 42 of the Pakistan Forest Act, 1927 (Act XVI of 1927) the Governor of
Baluchistan is pleased to make the following rules to regulate the cutting,
lopping, girdling and injuring by fire and removal of reserved trees.
1. Short title and extent.‑(1) These rules may be
called the Kalat Division Reserved Trees Rules, 1970.
(2) They shall come into force
at once.
(3) They shall extend to the
whole of Kalat Division.
2. Interpretation clause.‑In these rules unless there is
anything repugnant in the subject of the context, the following expressions
shall have the meanings hereby respectively assigned to them, that is to say:‑
(a) ."Conservator of
Forests" means the Conservator of Forests, Baluchistan.
(b) "Divisional Forest
Officer" means the Divisional Forest Officer Incharge of a Forest
Division.
(c) "Range Forest
Officer" means the Range Forest Officer, Incharge of a Forest Range.
(d) "Forest Act"
means Pakistan Forest Act, 1927 (XVI of 1927).
(e) "Reserved Trees"
means all kinds of trees reserved under these . rules and listed in Schedule I.
(f) "Offence" means
an offence punishable under these rules.
3. Prohibition for cutting etc.‑No person shall cut, collect or
remove timber or firewood of any reserved trees for sale except under a permit
and in accordance with the conditions thereof.
4. Application for permit.‑(1) Any person
desiring to cut, collect or remove timber or firewood of any reserved tree
shall apply in writing either directly to the Divisional Forest Officer or
through the Range Forest officer concerned for grant of a Permit.
(2) The Divisional Forest
Officer, may, subject to any of the conditions which may be imposed under these
rules issue a permit to the applicant for a period not exceeding seven days.
5. Power to refuse or revoke a permit.‑----(1)
The Divisional Forest Officer may, for reasons to be recorded in writing,
refuse to grant a permit or revoke a permit granted to a permit‑holder.
(2) Any person aggrieved by an
order refusing to grant a permit or revoking a permit may prefer an appeal to
the Conservator of Forests and thereupon the Conservator of Forests may
confirm, modify or rescind the orders of the Divisional Forest Officer or make
such orders as he may deem fit.
6. Payment of Royalty.‑
(1) Payment of royalty on the
timber and firewood of reserved trees cut, felled, removed or collected, shall
be made in advance at the rates given in Schedule It.
(2) If the firewood is allowed
to be converted into charcoal, the royalty payable in respect of the charcoal
so obtained .shall be three times the rates prescribed in respect of timber and
firewood under sub‑rule (1).
7. Restrictions on the transfer of permit.‑The permit‑holder
shall not transfer the permit to, or share it with, another person.
8. Power to inspect the permit.‑The permit‑holder
shall produce the permit for inspection, when called upon to do so, by any
Forest-Officer or Extra Assistant Commissioner or Tehsildar, any such officer
may stop for examination any timber or firewood of the reserved trees which is
in transit.
9. Surrender of permit.‑The permit shall, on the expiry of the
period for which it is granted, be returned at the Forest Check Post nearest to
the destination shown in the permit, whether the timber or firewood has been
removed or not.
10. Compliance with
instructions.‑A permit‑holder shall comply with the instructions of
the Forest Department as to the locality, mode of felling, conversion, removal,
or any other matter in respect of timber, or, at firewood of the reserved
trees.
